sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Carter County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Three offices share the work in Carter County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values your land and house, the county clerk prepares the bills and takes over unpaid ones, and the sheriff collects the tax during the payment season. All three sit in the old courthouse complex at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, which makes a single trip possible if you need answers on all of them.

The county is a long, mostly rural stretch of northeastern Kentucky. It covers about 412 square miles, was carved out of Greenup and Lawrence counties in 1838, and has two cities, Grayson (the seat) and Olive Hill. Most of the 12,206 housing units counted in the 2020 census sit outside those two towns, so most Carter County bills are for rural parcels, farm tracts and older frame houses.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Carter County tax questions?
sections.html:
Start with the office that matches the question: value goes to the PVA, a bill amount or payment goes to the sheriff, and anything already delinquent goes to the clerk. The county's official directory lists the details below.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the Carter County housing stock?
sections.html:
Carter County houses are mostly owner-occupied, and many are older. The 2020 census recorded 10,664 households, with 75.7 percent of occupied homes owned by the people living in them and 12.6 percent of all units vacant. Population was 26,627 that year, and the county's median age was 42.6.

That mix matters when you list. The county was a fire clay and refractory brick center in the early and mid 1900s, with plants at Olive Hill and Hitchins, and the old railroad corridors still shape where houses cluster. Interstate 64 and US 60 cross the county, so a property near either road is easier to reach than a hollow parcel on a county lane. Public schools come from the Carter County School District, and Kentucky Christian University sits in Grayson.

  • Carter Caves State Resort Park lies inside the county and brings seasonal visitors.
  • Grayson and Olive Hill are the only incorporated cities, so most properties are taxed as county parcels.
  • Large acreage and mobile home parcels follow the same bill and appeal rules as town lots.

sections.h2: When are Carter County property taxes due and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Kentucky's collection schedule applies in Carter County: bills go out around October 1, and the amount you owe changes with the date you pay. KRS 134.015 sets the steps.

  • Paid in full by November 1: a 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 through December 31: the face amount on the bill.
  • January 1 through 31: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After January 31: a 10 percent penalty, plus the sheriff's add-on fee.

Taxes are a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and a lien follows the parcel for eleven years whoever owns it. If a bill never arrives, call the sheriff at the number above. Ask the sheriff's office how it takes mailed and in-person payments.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Carter County assessment?
sections.html:
Ask the Carter County PVA for a conference first, because Kentucky law does not let you skip that step. KRS 133.120 requires the conference to happen before or during the public inspection of the tax roll, and the Department of Revenue says the roll is open for 13 days starting the first Monday in May.

If the conference does not settle it, file a written appeal with the county clerk no later than one workday after the inspection period closes. Your petition should name the property and state what you think it is worth. The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection ends and decides on evidence such as sales listings, construction costs and insurance policies. A decision from that board can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, but an owner who skips the county board or fails to show up loses that route.

One practical point: an appeal does not pause collection. Pay the tax on the value you claim while the case runs, and expect a supplemental bill if the final value is higher.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Carter County taxes after April 15?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate bills move from the sheriff to the county clerk on April 15 and become certificates of delinquency. The Carter County Clerk says the amount rises by roughly 40 percent once fees are added, and that personal checks are not taken on delinquent bills. Cash, money orders, company checks and cards (with a user fee) are accepted.

The clerk's office also offers a payment plan: one third down when the plan is set up, then 90 days to pay the rest. A plan that goes unpaid sends the bill back to the delinquent pile, and money already paid is not refunded but still counts toward the bill.

  • The clerk advertises delinquent bills about 30 days before the sale, in the local paper and on the clerk's website.
  • The 2024 delinquent sale was held August 29, 2025 at 10 am in the fiscal courtroom.
  • Buyers register with the clerk at least 10 days ahead, and a lien assignment costs $46.

Anyone who buys a certificate gains the right to collect from you, so the cheapest time to settle is before April 15, while only the sheriff's penalty applies.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Carter County?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who live in the home. The exemption is subtracted from the assessed value before tax is figured, and you apply at the Carter County PVA. The Department of Revenue lists the amount for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years at $49,100, so a house assessed at $120,000 would be taxed on $70,900. Ask the PVA what the current figure is, since the amount is reset every two years.

Age is proven with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims usually need yearly renewal unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has a permanent disability finding from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Carter County house when taxes are owed?
sections.html:
You can sell with taxes outstanding, because the amount owed is paid out of the sale price at closing. Before you list, ask the sheriff for a payoff on any current bill and ask the clerk whether older years sit in delinquency. A recorded certificate shows up in a title search and has to be paid or released before a buyer can take clean title.

Timing helps. A bill still with the sheriff carries only the 5 or 10 percent penalty. Once it reaches the clerk, fees and interest apply, so a quick sale in the first months of the year can save real money. If the house needs work, is inherited, or has a tenant, a buyer who purchases as-is can pay the tax lines from your proceeds so you do not have to bring cash to the table.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Carter County?
faqs.a: The sheriff collects it at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, phone (606) 474-5616. After April 15 the county clerk takes over unpaid bills.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Carter County bill by mail?
faqs.a: Ask the sheriff's office at (606) 474-5616 which payment methods it accepts and where to mail a check. Do not mail a payment before you have the correct address and your bill number.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Carter County assessment?
faqs.a: File with the county clerk by the end of the first workday after the roll inspection period ends. The inspection runs 13 days from the first Monday in May, and you must hold a PVA conference before filing.

faqs.q: Does Carter County take personal checks for delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's office says personal checks are not accepted on delinquent bills. Cash, money orders, company checks and cards work, and card payments carry a user fee.

faqs.q: Will back taxes stop me from selling a house in Carter County?
faqs.a: No, but they must be cleared at closing. Get a payoff figure from the sheriff or clerk, and the title company deducts it from your proceeds.
